newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica shares continue to sag on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica shares continue to sag on bourse.

text.p: Shares in Telefonica dragged the market down on Friday, extending the downtrend begun at the start of July after setting a record high of 4,665 pesetas, dealers and analysts said.

"For the past couple of weeks, shares in Telefonica have been performing badly in the bourse, but with an accumulated fall of 12 percent, we have begun to recommend reestabilishing positions," a fund manager said.

AT 1110 GMT, Telefonica shares were off 60 pesetas, or 1.44 percent, to 4,105 pesetas, slightly above the day's low of 4,090. It was underperforming the bourse, which was off just 4.45 points, or 0.07 percent, to 6,806.28.
"All in all recent news hasn't been favourable for Telefonica," a Spanish bank analyst said.

"The possible review of the merger of British Telecommunication and U.S.-based MCI, an alliance in which Telefonica forms part, and the recent moves by the company in the telecommunications sector, unclear short-term profitability, and worries about potential legal problems are the reasons behind the price correction for Telefonica," he added.
